title: Fourier Monomials Have Unit Norm
content: Proves that every Fourier monomial has unit norm: `fourier_norm_eq_one (n : Z) (x : AddCircle T) : ||fourier n x|| = 1`. Since `fourier n x = exp(2*pi*i*n*x/T)` lies on the unit circle, its complex modulus is 1. The proof reduces to `simp [fourier_apply]`, which unfolds the definition and applies Mathlib's norm lemma for unit-circle elements.
mathContext: $\|e_n(x)\| = |e^{2\pi i n x / T}| = 1$ for all $n \in \mathbb{Z}$ and $x \in \mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}$. This is the foundational bound from which the trivial bound $\|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| \le 2$ follows by the triangle inequality.

title: Trivial Bound: Fourier Mode Differences Bounded by 2
content: Proves `fourier_sub_norm_le_two`: the difference of two unit-norm complex exponentials has norm at most 2. The proof is a clean `calc` chain: apply `norm_sub_le` (triangle inequality), rewrite both norms to 1 via `fourier_norm_eq_one`, then close with `norm_num`. This bound is sharp (attained when `fourier n x` and `fourier n y` are antipodal) and is one of the two ingredients for the interpolation-based Holder bound.
mathContext: $\|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| \le \|e_n(x)\| + \|e_n(y)\| = 1 + 1 = 2$. This is the frequency-independent bound. Combined with the frequency-dependent Lipschitz bound $\|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| \le \frac{2\pi|n|}{T} d(x,y)$, the interpolation lemma yields the Holder bound.

title: Zero Mode Is Constant
content: Two results: `fourier_zero_eq_one` proves that the zeroth Fourier monomial is the constant function 1 (since `exp(0) = 1`), and `fourier_zero_sub` proves its difference vanishes: `fourier 0 x - fourier 0 y = 0`. Both follow by `simp [fourier_apply]` and `sub_self`. The zero mode is special because it contributes nothing to the Holder bound, so the main theorem sums only over `n != 0`.
mathContext: $e_0(x) = e^{0} = 1$ for all $x$, so $e_0(x) - e_0(y) = 0$. This means the $n=0$ term in the Fourier series contributes a constant to $f$ and does not affect the Holder modulus of continuity.

title: rpow_interpolation: The Key Analytic Tool
content:
Proves the interpolation lemma: if `0 <= a <= A` and `0 <= a <= B`, then `a <= A^(1-t) * B^t` for `t in [0,1]`. The proof splits into two cases. When `a = 0`, the bound holds trivially since `rpow` of nonneg values is nonneg. When `a > 0`, the proof factors `a = a^(1-t) * a^t` (via `rpow_add` and `rpow_one`), then applies `Real.rpow_le_rpow` to each factor: `a^(1-t) <= A^(1-t)` from `a <= A` and `a^t <= B^t` from `a <= B`, combining via `mul_le_mul`.

This is the central analytic result of the file -- it converts a pair of bounds (trivial + Lipschitz) into a single Holder-type bound.
mathContext: If $0 \le a \le A$ and $0 \le a \le B$, then $a = a^{1-t} \cdot a^t \le A^{1-t} \cdot B^t$ for $t \in [0,1]$. Applied with $a = \|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\|$, $A = 2$ (trivial bound), $B = L_n \cdot d(x,y)$ (Lipschitz bound), and $t = \alpha$, this yields the Holder bound $\|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| \le 2^{1-\alpha} \cdot L_n^\alpha \cdot d(x,y)^\alpha$.

title: Summability of Fourier Coefficients (Sorry)
content: States that if Fourier coefficients decay as `O(1/|n|^beta)` with `beta > 1`, then the coefficient norms are summable over Z. This is sorry'd. The proof outline decomposes Z into `{0}` union positive and negative integers, handles `n = 0` trivially, and reduces each half to the convergent p-series `sum 1/n^beta` via `Real.summable_nat_rpow_inv`. The main Mathlib gap is the need for a clean Z-to-N reduction of p-series summability.
mathContext: Need to show $\sum_{n \in \mathbb{Z}} \|\hat{c}_n\| < \infty$ given $\|\hat{c}_n\| \le C/|n|^\beta$ for $n \ne 0$ and $\beta > 1$. This reduces to $\sum_{n=1}^{\infty} 1/n^\beta < \infty$ (the $p$-series test with $p = \beta > 1$), applied to both positive and negative halves of $\mathbb{Z}$.

title: Fourier Mode Lipschitz Bound (Sorry -- Critical Path)
content: States `fourier_lipschitz_bound`: `||fourier n x - fourier n y|| <= 2*pi*|n|/T * dist x y`. This is the critical path sorry -- it is the frequency-dependent bound that, combined with the trivial bound via `rpow_interpolation`, yields the Holder bound. The proof requires showing that `exp(i*theta)` is 1-Lipschitz in theta, then composing with the linear map `x -> 2*pi*n*x/T`. Mathlib's `LipschitzWith` API for `toCircle` would provide the key ingredient.
mathContext: $\|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| = |e^{2\pi i n x/T} - e^{2\pi i n y/T}| = 2|\sin(\pi n (x-y)/T)| \le 2\pi|n|/T \cdot d(x,y)$. The inequality $|e^{i\alpha} - e^{i\beta}| \le |\alpha - \beta|$ (Lipschitz constant 1 for the exponential on the imaginary axis) is the core estimate.

title: Fourier Mode Holder Bound (Sorry)
content: States `fourier_holder_bound`: each Fourier monomial satisfies a Holder bound `||fourier n x - fourier n y|| <= 2^(1-alpha) * (2*pi*|n|/T)^alpha * dist(x,y)^alpha`. This follows directly from `rpow_interpolation` applied with A = 2 (from `fourier_sub_norm_le_two`) and B = (2*pi*|n|/T)*dist(x,y) (from `fourier_lipschitz_bound`), then factoring B^alpha = (2*pi*|n|/T)^alpha * dist^alpha. It is sorry'd because it depends on the unproved `fourier_lipschitz_bound`.
mathContext: Applying $a \le A^{1-\alpha} B^\alpha$ with $A=2$, $B = \frac{2\pi|n|}{T} d(x,y)$: $$\|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| \le 2^{1-\alpha} \left(\frac{2\pi|n|}{T}\right)^\alpha d(x,y)^\alpha.$$ The factor $|n|^\alpha$ will be absorbed when summing against $\|\hat{c}_n\| \le C/|n|^\beta$, yielding convergence when $\beta - \alpha > 1$.

title: dist-to-edist HolderWith Conversion (Sorry)
content: States `holderWith_of_dist_bound`: converts a dist-based Holder bound (`||f x - f y|| <= C * dist(x,y)^alpha` for all x, y) into Mathlib's `HolderWith C alpha f`, which uses `edist` (extended distance). The conversion requires `ENNReal.ofReal`/`toReal` manipulations and the relationship `edist x y = ENNReal.ofReal (dist x y)`. This is a technical sorry that involves no deep mathematics, just API plumbing between `dist` and `edist` in Mathlib.
mathContext: Mathlib's `HolderWith C \alpha f` means $\mathrm{edist}(f(x), f(y)) \le C \cdot \mathrm{edist}(x,y)^\alpha$ for all $x,y$, where edist is the extended nonneg real distance. The conversion from $\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le C \cdot d(x,y)^\alpha$ requires passing through `nndist` and `ENNReal.coe_rpow_of_nonneg`.

title: Main Theorem: Decay Implies Regularity (Sorry)
content:
States `decay_implies_regularity'`: if `f : C(AddCircle T, C)` has Fourier coefficients satisfying `||c_n|| <= C_decay / |n|^beta` for `n != 0` with `beta > alpha + 1`, then f is alpha-Holder continuous. The proof structure is visible in the sorry'd body: (1) summability from `summable_norm_fourierCoeff_of_decay`, (2) Fourier inversion from `hasSum_fourier_series_of_summable`, (3-6) bounding `||f(x) - f(y)||` by summing the Holder bounds over all modes, with convergence guaranteed by `beta - alpha > 1`.

The hypothesis `beta > alpha + 1` (rather than `beta > alpha`) reflects the Sobolev embedding gap on the circle: gaining alpha derivatives of regularity from Fourier decay requires spending 1/2 derivative to pass from L2 to C^0, and another 1/2 for the summability margin.
mathContext: $$\|\hat{c}_n\| \le \frac{C}{|n|^\beta},\; \beta > \alpha + 1 \implies f \in C^{0,\alpha}(\mathbb{R}/T\mathbb{Z}).$$ Proof sketch: $\|f(x) - f(y)\| \le \sum_n \|\hat{c}_n\| \cdot \|e_n(x) - e_n(y)\| \le \sum_n \frac{C}{|n|^\beta} \cdot 2^{1-\alpha} \left(\frac{2\pi|n|}{T}\right)^\alpha d^\alpha = K \cdot d^\alpha \cdot \sum_n |n|^{\alpha - \beta}$, which converges since $\beta - \alpha > 1$.

title: Proof Summary and Dependency Graph
content:
The closing summary documents the decomposition of the monolithic sorry in FourierSeriesOQ02.lean (line 403) into 5 independent sub-goals. The dependency structure forms a DAG:

- `fourier_lipschitz_bound` (independent, critical path)
- `fourier_holder_bound` depends on `fourier_lipschitz_bound` + proved `rpow_interpolation` + proved `fourier_sub_norm_le_two`
- `summable_norm_fourierCoeff_of_decay` (independent, needs Z p-series)
- `holderWith_of_dist_bound` (independent, API plumbing)
- `decay_implies_regularity'` depends on all four above + Fourier inversion

Resolving `fourier_lipschitz_bound` unblocks `fourier_holder_bound` and thereby `decay_implies_regularity'`, making it the critical path item.
mathContext: The DAG has depth 3: (level 0) proved lemmas `rpow_interpolation`, `fourier_sub_norm_le_two`; (level 1) independent sorries `fourier_lipschitz_bound`, `summable_norm_fourierCoeff_of_decay`, `holderWith_of_dist_bound`; (level 2) `fourier_holder_bound` depending on level 1; (level 3) `decay_implies_regularity'` assembling everything.
